sections.source_title: Temporal Projection, Precognition, and Causal-Calculus Canon
sections.reader_explanation: This section establishes the measurement vocabulary used by the later future-modeling system. It separates what a thinker can do (cognitive capacity) from how efficiently that capacity can be deployed (deployability/proficiency), while defining power, speed and agility for both cognition and metacognition. For Arthiteans, corresponding cognitive and metacognitive capacities are stated to share equal Lydrextent, making metathinking a matched higher-order companion rather than an unrelated skill-set.

This section defines Mul as a maximumless amount and then builds a confrontation taxonomy around hax and superhax. Hax bypass or invalidate ordinary statistics; superhax are the subset whose primary effects are metaeffects, meaning effects that directly act on other effects or their operation. It then separates depth, strength and breadth, uses those axes to define prowess/quality and power-skewity, and links hax/superhax growth factors to Arthitean physiology and instinct. The key distinction is categorical: a superhax is still hax, but not every hax is superhax and not every metaeffect-producing ability automatically qualifies as superhax.

This section turns ordinary forecasting into a recursively recalibrated ladder. A projected future is a forecast from a present information-state; each metaprojected layer forecasts from the recalibrated prior forecast. After a maximumless metaprojected depth, the ladder names the next stage hyperprojected future, with further hyperprojected orders continuing recursively. Hyperprecognition is then defined as maximumless capacity to perceive these hyperprojected layers at any future distance.

This section moves the projection logic from one future-line to a rewrite-indexed omniversal sequence. The Omnitimeline is an ordered succession of complete omniversal temporal states produced by causal-temporal rewrites; a transfuture is any later Omnitimeline state relative to a chosen reference index. Projected, metaprojected and hyperprojected transfutures repeat the recalibration ladder across this rewrite-space. An ultraprojected future is the complete hyperprojected-future structure contained in, corresponding to, or generated from a hyperprojected transfuture.
reader_notes: Do not collapse Omnitimeline into Parahistory: the later living-canon Parahistory masterpage is a rewrite-causal derivation graph, not merely an ordered temporal-state sequence.

sections.reader_explanation: This section makes future-knowledge operational. Outerprecognition covers flawless perception/memory of every ultraprojected future plus the future-content of Zeretic meditation. Zeretic meditation uses the irreducibility of a maximumless event-amount to remember more selected events than originally occurred, thereby rewriting history/outcome; a Zeren-operation applies this to one maximumless event-type. Zeretic calculation chooses operations while accounting for cascading effects, and causal-calculus applies that calculation to the ultraprojected future to make an optimal outcome necessary. The source universalizes this package to all Arthiteans and uses Dyvane/Qintara examples to show training/combat-history rewriting.

sections.source_title: Metaexpectation, Metagovernance, Antipossibility, and Lydrextent Canon
sections.reader_explanation: This opening node defines metaexpectation as an expectation about how far an expectation will be surpassed, and metaexpectation-surpassingness as the amount of that surpassing. The later Antipossibility and Lydrextent ladders use this surpassingness as their measured axis, so this section supplies the comparison-basis rather than the full ladder itself.

This section defines recursive governance-depth. Rules govern what is allowed, valid, possible or classifiable; Metarules govern rules; Metarules² govern Metarules, and the recursion continues without terminal order. Impossibility-governance is the particular rules/metarules structure controlling what can count as impossible. This governance stack is the formal prerequisite for Antipossibility: later sections do not merely posit “more impossible” magnitudes, but states that outrun classification at specified governance-depths.

This section defines intrafamily Antipossibility order. Antipossible is not “possible”; it is an extent that the rules of impossibility cannot even contain as impossible. Antipossible² shifts the failure upward to the Metarules governing those rules, with order n corresponding to impossibility-metagovernance depth n−1. The noncontainment is cumulative, so a higher order is not adequately represented by possibility, impossibility or any lower Antipossibility order.

This section adds an outer recursion above the within-family Antipossibility orders. A family contains a complete recursively ordered impossibility ladder; when that entire family becomes the governed object of a higher impossibility-governance basis, a new family begins. Family 1 is Antipossible, family 2 Outerantipossible and family 3 Transantipossible. Family-order has supremacy over intrafamily order: any state in family k+1 outranks every state in family k regardless of the lower family’s internal order.

Lydrextent compresses the two-dimensional Antipossibility coordinate into a diagonal scale. If A(k,n) denotes family k and intrafamily order n, then Lydrextent n is exactly A(n,n). Advancing one Lydrextent therefore raises both the outer family-order and inner Metarule-order simultaneously. This is why the source calls Lydrextent biordinal: it is not a single-axis magnitude ladder.
reader_notes: Canonical coordinate rule: Lydrextent n = A(n,n).

sections.reader_explanation: This section standardizes contest-result vocabulary instead of treating every superiority as generic “power.” Overpowering, outspeeding, outmaneuvering and outlasting identify which performance domain decides the interaction; outperforming is metric-general; overwhelmed is the broader failure to keep up/resist/prevail. Contest superiority differential measures the relative performance gap, while overwhelm gradient expresses the degree of overwhelming in Lydrextent terms.

This is a general conversion rule: for any performance metric X to which Lydrextent applies, Transcendent X means the Lydrextent of X. The listed strength, speed, agility, endurance, stamina, durability, reaction, processing and cognitive forms are examples of one reusable operator rather than unrelated abilities. Readers should therefore interpret “Transcendent” here as a measurement transform onto the Lydrextent scale.

This section defines performance/exertion by Antipossibility order rather than by Lydrextent’s two-axis diagonal. Transmodal-performance extent n is successful performance whose metaexpectation-surpassingness reaches Antipossibleⁿ but not the next order; Transmodal-exertion extent n applies the same ladder to healthy successful exertion. The source explicitly means literal mathematical/logical impossibility, not merely extreme difficulty.

This section distinguishes Transmodal-fitness from unlimited fitness categorically: unlimited fitness has no upper bound inside a possibility-space, whereas Transmodal-fitness succeeds at levels that the possibility-framework itself denies. Performance factor one measures Lydrextent of Transmodal-performance gained per physiological exertion; factor two measures Lydrextent of Transmodal-exertion gained per effort. The state is framed as healthier at higher impossible/antipossible performance and is applied explicitly to Rhayhara’s physical, mental and spiritual prowess.

This legacy-labelled source block begins with metaskill and then records the Omniprefixal Hyperenglish/Ultraenglish construction rules used by the edited Divine corpus. Compoterms combine precise prefixes, English roots and functional English suffixes; Hyperenglish prioritizes semantic precision and compression; Ultraenglish additionally uses that system to metainvent roots. The Omniprefixal extension permits globally sourced prefix-operators only when they add reversible, stable semantic value, while explicit gates preserve established canon ladder-prefixes and reject decorative exoticism.

sections.reader_explanation: This section governs how new terminology should be engineered. Root-vetting checks whether a root behaves cleanly under prefixes, suffixes, recursion, negation and scope; metaroot-vetting applies similar scrutiny to the definition-logic itself. Prefixes and suffixes must add a specific semantic function, and the anti-noise rule rejects morphology that merely sounds stronger. The overall goal is shortest semantically complete compoterm-family definitions without sacrificing axis precision.

This is a decoding key for compacted terms used later in Divine v144. It defines Greater-Orders as the self-governing conceptual structure that determines identity, interpretation, admissibility and subordinate order; it then supplies compact forms for permission-depth, performance, force-type, causal-attributability, bloodline-blessing language and several legacy replacements. The audit notes are editorial provenance: they record systematic conversion passes and preservation limits rather than introducing independent world mechanics.

sections.source_title: Section 1: Master Definitions-First Glossary Unaxiomatic Laddering Unaxiom =
sections.reader_explanation: This begins the definitions-first glossary with the Unaxiomatic ladder. An Unaxiom is a foundational rule a system treats as false without requiring a deeper disproof inside that system. A Meta-Unaxiom is a higher-order axiom or governing rule about Unaxioms; Meta-unaxiomatic² governs Meta-Unaxioms, Meta-unaxiomatic³ governs the preceding meta-level, and the source explicitly continues the recursion without a terminal level. The important reading distinction is that these are recursively higher governance statements about what is treated as false, not merely larger quantities of ordinary falsity.

sections.source_title: Subcategory: Definition Format Rule Definition Format Rule = the rule that detected definitions are written in the format '[term] is [definition]' or '[terms] are [definition]' wherever possible, with absolute minimal editing to avoid distorting precise meaning.
sections.reader_explanation: The heading itself contains the complete rule. When a definition is detected, it should be normalized into an explicit ‘term is definition’ or ‘terms are definition’ construction wherever possible, but edits must remain absolutely minimal so the original precise meaning is not distorted. This is an editorial preservation rule that explains the standardized wording seen in the glossary; it does not authorize paraphrasing away source detail.
reader_notes: This rule reinforces source preservation: formatting may be standardized, but semantic content should not be compressed or replaced.
